findings.description: Doc-vs-code drift introduced by (or already present prior to) the fix-pass: V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md item 15.a at line 1263 claims `pub struct Spec` carries '`#[non_exhaustive]` already APPLIED — KEEP', and Section 11 (item 11 sweep table) row 916 lists `benten-core::subgraph_spec::Spec` as YES `#[non_exhaustive]` + 'KEEP'. Ground-truth at HEAD: `crates/benten-core/src/subgraph_spec/spec.rs:189-190` declares `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]` followed immediately by `pub struct Spec { ... }` — NO `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute. The line-125 `#[non_exhaustive]` in the same file belongs to the sibling `pub enum SubgraphSpecRestriction` (line 126); the only other occurrence is at line 111 inside a docstring. Practical SemVer impact is NIL because `Spec` has all-private fields (`roots`, `edges`, `inclusion`, `max_depth`) + `pub fn builder() -> SpecBuilder` (line 216) + read-only accessor methods — external direct-struct-literal construction is already blocked by visibility. But the freeze-doc CLAIM is factually wrong + the audit-test pin at `crates/benten-engine/tests/g_core_9_non_exhaustive_audit.rs` does NOT exercise Spec's attribute presence (it covers AuthorizationGrant / GrantKeyMaterial / UcanEnvelope / ManifestVerifyMode / Strategy carve-out + others, but NOT Spec). This is a §3.6j sweep-completeness-self-verify violation: the doc claims a sweep coverage the code doesn't honor. Two valid closures: (a) APPLY `#[non_exhaustive]` to `pub struct Spec` (additive at v1-beta since direct construction was already blocked; aligns the bytes with the doc claim; ~1 LOC), OR (b) RETENSE the doc claims at 15.a:1263 + table row 916 to read 'private-fields-+-builder pattern provides equivalent SemVer-safety; #[non_exhaustive] not required' (~5 LOC). Per Fork 1 / Fork 2 fix-pass precedent (doc-tighten when the code is intentional), option (b) is the lower-risk path; but if the freeze contract treats Section 11's table as the binding inventory, option (a) is the spec-literal close.

R1-r1-5 carryover NOT CLOSED at the fix-pass despite triage §3 sub-bundle D listing it as FIX-NOW Bundle 7 (doc-coupling drift sweep): V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE.md item 15.c at lines 1363-1366 still reads 'Wire envelope typed for additive future arms via codepoint-dispatch (same playbook as crypto-agility per CLAUDE.md #5) — i.e. a future arm lands at a NEW codepoint, never repurposing the existing two-arm enum.' Ground-truth: `crates/benten-caps/src/scope.rs:25-52` continues to use plain `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub enum Scope` with two arms `Hashes(Vec<Cid>)` + `RestrictedSelector(RestrictedScope)` — serde-tag dispatch only, NO `pub mod codepoint` table parallel to the encryption_class.rs:57 / SigCodepoint / HashCodepoint pattern. The serde-tagged-enum IS additive-friendly so the freeze contract is not BROKEN, but the 'codepoint-dispatch' phrasing implies a numeric-table machinery that isn't there. Spec §1.A.FROZEN item 15(c) carries the same phrasing — this is plan-doc + contract-doc parallel drift. Per the R1 triage's own disposition (FIX-NOW Bundle 7), this should have landed; the fix-pass diff shows zero edits to the codepoint-dispatch language. Two valid closures: (a) DOWNGRADE the language to 'serde-tag dispatch' (~3 LOC edit at both 15.c + plan §134), OR (b) ADD a `pub mod codepoint` typed-reject machinery alongside EncryptionClass's pattern (~30 LOC delivering on the explicit claim). (a) is the lower-risk path consistent with how 15.c's NO-#[non_exhaustive] carve-out structurally constrains the enum.

Triage doc factual asymmetry (forensic-context observation, not a freeze-contract issue): the R1 fix-pass commit message + the brief framing claim 'L17-r1-2 grant types #[non_exhaustive] escalated to G-COMP-1 Row D-17 per HARD RULE 12 clause-(b)' — but ground-truth at HEAD shows L17-r1-2 was CLOSED-AT-FIX-PASS, NOT deferred: `crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:73/175/232` all carry `#[non_exhaustive]` on UcanEnvelope / GrantKeyMaterial / AuthorizationGrant respectively, AND `crates/benten-engine/tests/g_core_9_non_exhaustive_audit.rs:127-137` pins the construction discipline via `GrantKeyMaterial::synthetic_for_test` / `from_bytes_for_test` helpers. Row D-17 in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md actually covers a DIFFERENT type set (`CapWriteContext` + `ReadContext` + `SuspensionOutcome` per L6-r1-1, with ~80+ test-site cascade). The brief's narrative conflates L17-r1-2 with L6-r1-1; the work-product is correct (Bundle 3 closed L17-r1-2, Row D-17 defers L6-r1-1) but the brief description doesn't match. This is OUT-OF-SCOPE for L17's freeze-question per HARD RULE 12 clause-(a) (it's a triage-narrative accuracy issue, not a freeze surface).
